title: wt remove <work> --yes --json
description: What `wt remove <work>` did, effect by effect. Printed by `wt remove <work> --yes --json` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the run. Where the worktree and the quarantine are is read from the disk when the object is written. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

repo.description: The main checkout; null outside a repository.

trunkSource.description: Since 1.3.0. How trunk was found, as in the other plans (see docs/json.md, trunkSource); null with trunk.

token.description: The token of the plan this run made; with --expect, the one it was held to.

outcome.description: removed: the worktree is gone, or quarantined, and the branch step did what the plan said. removedWithBranchProblem: the worktree is gone and the branch was left as it was on purpose (it moved, is no longer merged, or a worktree took it); error says which. refused: nothing changed; problems says why. partial: something changed and a later step failed — a quarantine that stopped after writing recovery.json, the second move, or the branch step; the steps and quarantine say which, and restoreCommand undoes a quarantine. interrupted: a signal ended the run.

problems.description: For refused: why, as the plan names it, and planChanged for --expect.

branch.description: The branch the plan read; null when detached.

steps.description: worktree, branch and superset, in that order.

forced.description: Since 1.2.0. The --force categories the removal went past, in the plan or in the sessions and checkout read again right before the checkout went; empty when it went past none or did not get that far.

quarantine.description: With --quarantine, once its recovery.json is written.

restoreCommand.description: The argv that puts back what went: wt restore <dir> once a quarantine wrote its recovery.json; since 1.4.0 wt refs restore <runId> --only refs/heads/<name> --yes for a branch moved into a pin; else git branch <name> <tip> for a branch gone from its name (renamed to keepAs); null when nothing needs it.

runId.description: Since 1.4.0. The run under refs/wt-swept/ the deleted branch was moved into, as wt refs sweep moves backups: wt refs swept lists it, wt refs restore puts it back, wt refs purge deletes it for good. null when the branch was not moved: renamed, untouched, kept, or deleted by a quarantine, which pins it itself. A run a signal ended may name a run that holds only its meta.

code.description: dirty: anything uncommitted, submodules included, or a submodule not at its recorded commit. statusUnknown: git status, the git dir or HEAD could not be read. session: an agent session is in it, idle or busy. sessionsUnknown: the sessions could not be listed. lockHeld: git's worktree lock, and its holder is still running. operation: a rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in progress. hiddenChanges: files git status is told not to look at. headUnreachable: HEAD holds commits no surviving ref or worktree would. reachUnknown: what would be lost could not be worked out. submoduleUnreachable: a submodule commit only this worktree's copy holds. nestedWorktree: another worktree is inside it. quarantineUnusable: the --quarantine folder exists, is on another volume, or is inside the repository. planChanged (result only): --expect named another plan. The codes shared with sweep-plan's kept mean the same there.

force.description: --force goes past it: somebody's claim on the checkout, not work that would be lost.

forceWith.description: Since 1.2.0. The --force category that goes past it; null when force is false. A session problem is either idle-sessions or busy-sessions: idle and busy sessions are two problems.

forceCategory.description: What --force=<list> names; bare --force is all of them. idle-sessions: an idle agent session in it. busy-sessions: a busy one, and idle ones too. sessions-unknown: the sessions could not be listed. hidden-files: files git status is told not to look at, unedited. lock: git's lock, its holder still running.

result.description: worktree: removed, quarantined (both moves done), partlyMoved (the checkout moved, its admin dir not), kept (still there). branch: deleted, renamed (to keepAs), untouched, kept (turned down on purpose), failed (git failed). superset: deregistered, notRegistered, skipped, failed, optedOut (since 1.1.0: --keep-superset; Superset was not asked). Any: notRun (not reached), interrupted (a signal caught it and its state does not say it finished).

commit.description: For branch: the tip the plan read.

pin.description: Since 1.4.0. For branch: the ref the deleted branch was moved into, refs/wt-swept/<runId>/heads/<name>, read back holding commit; null otherwise.

steps.description: The removal's steps as recovery.json records them; empty when it has none.
